steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 baking sheets.
Whisk flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and cloves together in a bowl until well combined. Set aside.
Wrap zucchini in a clean towel; wring out to remove any excess moisture. Set aside.

Beat brown sugar and butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until creamy; beat in egg and vanilla extract. Stir in flour mixture and oats until just incorporated. Stir in zucchini and raisins until evenly combined. Drop rounded teaspoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until bottom edges turn golden brown, 14 to 16 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Zucchini Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This spicy zucchini oatmeal cookie recipe is flavored with warm cinnamon and spicy cloves and packed with heart-healthy oats and raisins for a sweet treat.
raw_recipe.name: Spicy Zucchini Oatmeal Cookies

review.reviewBody: These cookies turned out awesome- but I made a lot of changes. Before adding the zucchini I let it sit with some salt for 30 mins to get the extra moisture out, but that made my batter was too dry so I added another egg. Then I used pumpkin pie spice instead of straight cloves, and with the raisins I tossed in a handful each of pumpkin seeds, pecan pieces and coconut. I ended up with about 4 dozen soft, perfectly golden and very tasty cookies. I may never make them again though, because I can't stop eating them.

Turned out great! We like things less sweet so I cut the sugar in half. Pressing the zucchini slightly to remove some of the excess water helped to avoid making them overly moist. They will turn kind of cakey and can be had for breakfast.

Spicy Zucchini Oatmeal Cookie Haiku: "The taste was quite good, but baked up like 'muffin top', breakfast or dessert?" Recipe submitter says to drop these by rounded Teaspoonfuls which wasn't at all possible at all due to the sticky, clumpy oat-ey texture w/ the zucchini and raisins (oh, incidentally, I used 1/4 c. raisin, 1/4 c. chocolate chip) so I made mine into rather large balls, which baked into what I can only describe as resembling a muffin top. Many other reviews mention it being cakey, which is absolutely true so I found that these veered more towards a breakfast treat. To make these breast-feeding-friendly, I also added 1 TB brewer's yeast, 1 TB wheat germ, and half coconut oil for the butter. Very tasty right out of the oven yum yum!

First I doubled the recipe 
I added 1/2 tsp of salt. Extra cinnamon. Extra vanilla I used 1/2 c butter with 1/2 c shortening. I used Old Fashion Oats and No raisins for grandkids, but Grammie got extra in hers! Turned out amazing. Yummy!

Made for a potluck at my school with garden zucchini. I doubled the zucchini, didn't squeeze out any excess water (they were nice and moist and fluffy), added a bit of salt, semisweet morsels instead of raisins, and some walnuts. Would be good with butterscotch chips, too. Very good. Was the first dessert gone and many asked for recipe.

Good flavor. I loved the spiciness. I peeled--because I didn't want the zucchini to be so obvious ;-) -- and grated the zucchini but did not dry it off. The consistency of the cookies was almost more like a muffin than a cookie. I might try adding a bit of salt to activate the baking soda and maybe make the cookies a little lighter. I might also try substituting some grated carrots for the zucchini to give it a "carrot cake" vibe.

I had a larger zucchini, so I took out the seeds before shredding in food processor. Then I didn't take moisture out as recommended but used right away. Came out with a more moist cookie than 1st time I made these.

Great recipe and my 10 yr old says its her new favourite! The cookies were very soft & the spices were just right. Unfortunately I didn't have raisins on hand so used a bag of semi-sweet chocolate chips and we cannot wait to try it with raisins as per original recipe. Thanks for our new family favourite cookie :)
Added 1 cup of craisins instead of the 1/2 cup of raisins it called for

Love this recipe, will probably become a regular staple around here. However, I felt like the flavor was missing something, so the second time I made this, I added ginger (same amount as the cinnamon) and that did the trick! They’re also great to cook after freezing the dough, so I can cook them in smaller batches and have more in the freezer for more later.

I had a good feeling about these cookies even before I baked them. The spicy cake like texture combined with oats and in my case the addition of a few mini chocolate chips made for a very good cookie. The cloves are key for me in this recipe…I did add a pinch of salt and tried to squeeze out some moisture from the zucchini…. I wish I made a double batch…. Next time!!!
I liked the recipe but I added ginger and nutmeg. I always have to add my flavor to everything I cook
I didn't get the spice flavor. The only thing I changed was I used Pumpkin Pie Spice as suggested by others. I was a little disappointed that the cookies weren't sweeter.

Delicious cookie! Flavorful with the right amount of spices. After reading some of the comments, I did not remove the excess moisture from the zucchini and they turned out great. I will be making these again!
Good basic recipe, I used walnuts due to not having raisins and it was good. Will definitely save this recipe.
I made only one change and that is I used pumpkin pie spice instead of cloves. These are the best cookies ever!
Way to dry!! I even added a second egg. Next time I would not drain the zucchini and I would probably add additional liquid.
Quite tasty, but definitely needs some salt—maybe 1/2 t. I substituted chocolate chips for the raisins.
Didn't change a thing, and they came out wonderfully!
I really liked these, I used craisins instead of raisins and added chopped walnuts because I love nuts! Hubby thought they needed more craisins. Nice soft cookie. Loved the spice flavor.
